newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends weaker on late dlr-buying.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends weaker on late dlr-buying.

text.p: The Philippine peso closed slightly lower after some foreign banks started buying the U.S. currency in late afternoon, traders said.
"There was some activities in the afternoon, especially after London opened," a senior trader at a foreign bank said, although he said he was not aware of any reason for the dollar-buying.
The peso closed at 26.40 to the dollar from 26.397

The dollar was well-offered in the morning, as some investors shifted back into pesos after the speculative attack had abated and the Philippine Central Bank kept its benchmark overnight rate at a high of 30 percent.
The Central Bank raised its rate to 30 percent on Monday after the peso was hit by another round of speculative attack.
Earlier, the peso rose to an intra-day high of 26.396, with the Central Bank buying value-today dollars at 26.384 and 26.385 and value-tomorrow dollars at 26.397 to 26.399.
Traders said the Central Bank might have bought more than $200 million out of the $541 million traded throughout the day.
"We have active two-way quotes for the peso," another trader said.
While some traders were unloading their dollars in favour of the higher-yielding pesos, some were still wary about the short-term outlook of the local currency.
"There are still fears over the stability of the peso. Some so-called experts are still saying that the peso is still overvalued at this point," the foreign bank trader said.
The peso was expected to be the next target of speculators after last week's de facto devaluation of the Thai baht.
